children: The FTSE MIB was flat to slightly lower around 52,000 on Monday as investors tracked Middle East developments.
The US and Iran continued to exchange strikes, with Tehran threatening to establish a new restricted zone outside the Strait of Hormuz.
Attention also turned to the ECB's expected rate hike later this week as the conflict keeps oil prices elevated and fuels inflation concerns.
Among laggards, Telecom Italia (-1.1%), Enel (-0.8%) and Poste Italiane (-0.9%) traded lower.
In contrast, Eni climbed 1.5% as crude oil prices rose, while Tenaris and Saipem each added 1.7%.
Technology shares also outperformed, with STMicroelectronics (+2.3%) and Prysmian (+1.9%) tracking a global tech rally.

Financial stocks were little changed after Economy Minister Giancarlo Giorgetti reiterated the government's neutral stance on the M&A battle for MPS, saying the Treasury would retain its 4.9% stake until the process concludes.

title: FTSE MIB Flat at Start of Week
